CONTRACT COMPARISON vs get_duplicate_v1 (both read-only, both take {project_id, duplicate_id} on nearly the same path): the two descriptions ARE clearly distinguishing here, so this is not one of the unlabeled near-duplicate pairs. get_duplicate_v1 reads a currently 'suggested' pair — both full test cases side by side (title, description, folder, owner, ai_score, reason, duplicate_type), unwrapped at the top level as `duplicate`, intended for a human deciding how to resolve it; it 404s ({errors: 'Duplicate not found.'} or {errors:'Test case not found.'}, key 'errors' plural) once the pair has already been resolved. get_duplicate_source_test_case_v1 reads a pair that has ALREADY been merged — it returns not the live pair but the frozen pre-merge snapshot of the test case that was folded away, wrapped under `data.test_case`, with its own field set captured at merge time (steps, attachments with freshly-signed short-lived URLs, template) rather than reflecting the live test case; its 404 envelopes use the singular key 'error' and come in two shapes distinguished by presence of `data` (missing-snapshot vs unknown/unmerged). So the pair is not actually ambiguous/near-duplicate in the tracked-problem sense: one is 'inspect a live suggestion', the other is 'recover what a merge overwrote' — disjoint statuses (suggested vs merged), disjoint envelopes (top-level `duplicate` vs `data.test_case`), disjoint error key casing (`errors` vs `error`).
